summary: The global marketing team is in a critical push to launch the Intelligent China program and finalize the knowledge website redesign, while resolving urgent IT and follow-up tasks from the Tech in Asia Conference.
summaryDetail: The top priority this week is the Intelligent China program: the webpage must go live, with Module 1 (Beijing, Dec 1–4, 2026, EV & Intelligent Mobility) as the marketing and sales focus. Simultaneously, the knowledge website redesign is nearing completion—Joseph must share the HTML file, and the team needs to meet to provide final feedback to Joker for implementation. Immediate attention is also required for Tech in Asia Conference follow-ups: creating touch points, drafting a combined thank-you and program email, and saving the participant list. Looking ahead, the team must audit conversion tracking, analyze participant profiles, and draft October priorities for website, SEM/SEO, GEO, and content, while also advancing the Asia Start spotlight article and videos. The recent Outlook account lock issue has been resolved, but team members should verify password updates on all devices.

decisions.text: Remove the videos panel and integrate videos into topics instead of having a separate category.
Keep the two-menu structure with 'Knowledge' and 'School' menus, but decide on alignment (centered vs. left) later.
Display more articles on the homepage, similar to an editorial style, and consider adding a 'spotlight' section.
Bring indices (BCI, BSI, CKGSB) more prominently onto the knowledge homepage, possibly with a banner.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for marketing efforts.
Put US partnership programs on hold for the first quarter.
Consider Berkeley program as a third priority for audit phase.
Send one email to Tech in Asia Conference participants that includes both appreciation and program information, rather than separate thank-you and follow-up emails
